title: Modeled interruption preserves recovery-state obligations
statement: Every interruption-sensitive modeled operation MUST preserve its declared recovery-state obligations across supported independently durable effect boundaries and MUST NOT restart non-idempotent work unsafely.
rationale: Process interruption can expose intermediate durable state even when normal execution reaches a coherent final state, and recovery can duplicate effects when it blindly reruns uncertain work.
failure_prevented: Forbidden intermediate durable states, absent recovery continuations, false atomicity assumptions, or unsafe restart of non-idempotent external work.
applicability: Environment Contract v1 operations explicitly marked interruption-sensitive with ATOMIC, NON_ATOMIC, or UNKNOWN effect-group semantics. Unmodeled durability and concurrency remain uncertainty.
evaluation: Fortress introduces PROCESS_INTERRUPTED only between declared semantic effect steps, checks reachable recovery continuations and permitted/forbidden states, and reconciles restart behavior with operation idempotency.

finding.message: A modeled interruption or restart path violates declared recovery-state obligations.

remediation: Add a reachable recovery continuation, preserve only permitted durable states, or establish truthful atomicity/idempotency without hiding interruption uncertainty.
valid_example: Interruption between non-atomic durable steps reaches a recovery handler that returns the object to an explicitly permitted prior or completed state.
invalid_example: Multiple durable steps have no recovery path, or restart repeats a non-idempotent operation after uncertain completion.
exception_policy: Fortress does not infer durability, transactions, or atomicity from names. Unsupported storage and concurrency semantics remain explicit non-evidence.
history: Introduced with bounded semantic interruption points, recovery obligations, and trusted environmental atomicity.
